q.stem: A driver says, "The Road Users' Code is a law book, so breaking any piece of advice in it means I can be prosecuted." Which statement best explains the mistake in the driver's reasoning?
options: Everything in the Code is a law, so any breach of its advice can be prosecuted.
The Code is only a set of tips and has no connection to any law at all.
Some rules in the Code are also laid down by law, and the precise legal wording is found in the listed Ordinances, Regulations and Bylaws rather than in the Code itself.
The Code replaces the Ordinances, so its own wording is the only legal wording that applies to road users.
q.explanation: The Code says that some of its rules are also laid down by law, and that the exact wording of the law should be checked in the Ordinances, Regulations and Bylaws it lists. The Code also contains safety advice and guidance that goes beyond the law.
q.source_quote: Some of the rules are also laid down by law.
